cohort: The study included 7,783 admitted asphyxiated neonates at Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Center in Northern Tanzania between 2000 and 2022.
finding: The study observed a significant increase in the trends of in-hospital survival from birth asphyxia, rising from 68% in 2000 to 80% in 2022.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was identified as an independent significant predictor of in-hospital survival, with an Adjusted Hazard Ratio (AHR) of 1.69.
followup_time: N/A (follow-up was for in-hospital survival, with a median survival time of 4 days)
birth_weight: Measured as a variable and identified as a predictor of survival.
gest_age: Measured as a variable and identified as a predictor of survival.
